strings.name: Sepp Hochreiter
strings.role: Computer scientist, JKU Linz professor and NXAI co-founder
strings.summary: Hochreiter studies long-term dependencies and learning in neural networks. He analyzed vanishing gradients and developed LSTM with Jürgen Schmidhuber, then pursued machine learning, bioinformatics and AI in Linz. Recent team research includes xLSTM, the TiRex time-series model and industrial applications.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: He co-developed long short-term memory networks, advancing long-sequence modeling in speech, language and time-series analysis.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Computer science Diplom and doctorate, Technical University of Munich; also studied mathematics.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Learning long-term dependencies
strings.highlights.h1.text: His gradient analysis exposed difficulties in deep and recurrent networks; with Schmidhuber he developed memory cells and gating for LSTM, within a wider collaborative field.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Continuing recurrent-model research
strings.highlights.h2.text: With multiple collaborators he proposed xLSTM and TiRex for scalable language modeling and time-series forecasting; experimental results have specific tasks and test conditions.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discussing AI’s next phase
strings.timeline.t1.text: At FAU he discussed xLSTM, TiRex and robot memory; organizers subsequently posted a recording. These directions remain ongoing research.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Publishing the TiRex preprint
strings.timeline.t2.text: With Andreas Auer and collaborators, he introduced an xLSTM-based time-series foundation model for zero-shot short- and long-horizon forecasting.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Publishing the xLSTM preprint
strings.timeline.t3.text: The team presented extended LSTM architectures using exponential gating and different memory structures for large-scale sequence modeling.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Co-founding NXAI
strings.timeline.t4.text: He helped establish the company incorporated in December 2023, followed by a JKU research partnership aimed at industrial applications.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Leading the LIT AI Lab
strings.timeline.t5.text: He began directing the Linz Institute of Technology’s AI laboratory, connecting machine learning with interdisciplinary research.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becoming a professor in Linz
strings.timeline.t6.text: After work in Munich, Colorado and Berlin, he became JKU professor of bioinformatics, later leading its machine learning institute.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Co-authoring LSTM
strings.timeline.t7.text: With Schmidhuber, he published long short-term memory in Neural Computation, providing an important architecture for learning long sequences.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Early neural-network thesis
strings.timeline.t8.text: His Munich Diplom thesis analyzed dynamic neural-network training and gradient problems, forming an early foundation for his long-dependency research.
